characters.description: A formidable fighter whose primordial nature and return to Harwatch threaten the Archon's plans. He is tied to the Nemean legacy and stands among the few people the newly freed construct considers a serious obstacle.
characters.name: Felix Nevarre

characters.description: Felix's bonded Tenku companion, linked closely to his survival and able to aid him both directly and through their shared spiritual connection. Pit is an established partner rather than a mount or pet, and the bond makes each central to the other's safety.
characters.name: Pit

characters.description: A speaking chimera who guards a Foglands valley alongside an older companion. When a formerly active mountain domain falls unnaturally silent and then ruptures, A'zek investigates the danger, retreats from the creatures spilling out, and seeks to warn the Henaari.
characters.name: A'zek

characters.description: A golden armored construct that breaks free of confinement beneath a mountain. It commands Archids, postpones an attack on Harwatch while Felix remains there, and sends its forces to find a temple hidden behind a waterfall.
characters.name: The Archon

characters.description: A Cantus Sodalus chanter who has used the identity Anna and a changed appearance. She mentors Felix, reports his unusual condition to her order, and learns that surviving Inquisition members intend to report Harwatch's fall in Setoria.
characters.name: Zara Cyrene

characters.description: A sigilder who assists Felix with restoring Harwatch’s damaged wall arrays. He is married to Nia and is Amaya’s father.
characters.name: Hector

characters.description: A spear-wielding ally of Felix who leads rescue work in damaged Harwatch. Her heightened perception locates trapped survivors and hidden threats, while her manifested weapons help contain monsters emerging beneath the city.
characters.name: Vessilia Dayne

characters.description: A highly mobile fighter in Felix's circle who is advancing her inner training while Harwatch recovers. Her effort to untangle an Acrobatics-related obstruction in her core leaves her with severe pain but marks real progress.
characters.name: Evie Aren

characters.description: A scarred veteran who trains Evie and answers Cal's call during Harwatch's rebuilding. He brings hard-earned combat experience to the city's defense effort and expects demanding inner work from those he teaches, even when the process is painful.
characters.name: Harn

characters.description: The Lady of Harwatch and holder of the city's territorial authority. She is still learning the damaged seat's functions when a territory quest directs her to eliminate an unidentified hostile neighbor.
characters.name: Cal

characters.description: A fire mage and sigildry specialist who works with Alistair on Harwatch's defenses and waterworks planning as the damaged city prepares for further threats. He joins the discussion when Cal's new territory quest forces Harwatch to choose how it will answer danger beyond its walls.
characters.name: Atar V'as

characters.description: A fellow sigildry specialist who works with Atar V'as. He assists with the magical and practical planning needed to restore Harwatch's defenses and water system, then takes part in Cal's council as the city weighs the Archon against the threat of an Inquisition report.
characters.name: Alistair

characters.description: A Haarguard spearman involved in Harwatch's rebuilding and defense. He works alongside Bodhi and Yan in the city's newly organized guard as Cal confronts a territory quest and the possibility of enemies approaching from more than one direction.
characters.name: Kelgan

characters.description: A Haarguard trainee who watches Felix enter Harwatch Manor's golem chamber and ask to face its strongest constructs without weapons.
characters.name: Kylar

characters.description: A Haarguard trainee present when Felix challenges the training facility's most dangerous available golems. Nevia is part of the new city guard being developed while Harwatch restores its defenses and prepares for threats outside the damaged walls.
characters.name: Nevia

characters.description: A Haarguard trainee who observes Felix enter the manor's golem chamber to test himself against its constructs. Kikri belongs to the developing city guard, whose members are training while Harwatch rebuilds and faces the prospect of another major attack.
characters.name: Kikri

characters.description: A Haarguard trainee introduced among the guards who witness Felix test his strength against Harwatch Manor's golems. Vyne Pallas is part of the force Cal is building to defend Harwatch as the city's damaged arrays and breached wall are restored.
characters.name: Vyne Pallas

characters.description: A lost divine power connected to Felix through a shard he took from her. The fragment is embedded in his altered development and reacts within his two named cores, but its effect on his weaving stage and the changes caused by his primordial nature remain uncertain.
characters.name: Vellus

characters.description: The Duke of Pax Rell's Hand and Vessilia Dayne's appointed protector. Although still recovering, he trains and insists that his standing orders require him to escort Vess home now that she has reached Journeyman tier.
characters.name: Darius Reed

characters.description: A Fiend’s Legion recruit in the Blades faction who wants to defend Harwatch rather than simply follow Felix.
characters.name: Mervin Cors

characters.description: A Henaari far hunter who draws on Raven-linked power. She mistakes Felix's expedition for allies of the Reforged and attacks, but survives the clash and accepts a parley after a larger enemy force intervenes.
characters.name: Wyvora

characters.description: A Henaari guard at the concealed sanctuary. She helps confront and detain Felix after Wyvora guides his wounded party through the settlement's layered illusions and defenses. Felix's refusal to be separated from his companions brings him into direct conflict with her group.
characters.name: Ifre

characters.description: A Henaari figure whose companion, A'zek, ensures that Felix's wounded party receives guest protection and healing before taking Felix to meet him.
characters.name: The Far Walker

characters.description: An Urge revered by the Henaari and driven to seek hidden or lost things. It receives Felix inside a dangerous trial realm, accepts objects he uncovers as offerings, and then demands the key he carries.
characters.name: The Endless Raven

characters.description: The immense, failing spirit tree within the Nevis vault. Attuned to life, water, light, and shadow, the Caryatid Anima stands immobile when Felix first encounters it and tries to reach it through Communion.
characters.name: Caryatid Anima

characters.description: An ancient Nym guardian awakened in the ruined Nevis vault. Though corrosion has left his Eidolon body immobile, he recognizes Felix as the site's inheritor and offers guidance and service. A stored memory identifies him as the mortal Paragon who voluntarily became this guardian.
characters.name: Karys Taiv

characters.description: A mountainous void predator with many maws and a corrupt crimson mana signature. Its arrival scatters lesser creatures as it begins hunting Zara Cyrene's vulnerable company in a liminal passage.
characters.name: Whalemaw

characters.description: A figure connected to the mud-covered Muckminder that guards a bone bridge. When Felix destroys the guardian's artificial core, he preserves a memory from Vvim but has not yet examined it.
characters.name: Vvim

recaps.ending: Felix survives the omen path by resisting Vellus's attempt to force his advancement and forging the Path of the Cardinal Fiend. With the Endless Raven's help, he consumes the six Urges beneath the temple, becomes a Greater Primordial of the Unseen Tide, and defeats the Archon. Felix separates the former Unbound from the Archonic Construct, but the man's ultimate state remains uncertain after the Seed of Remembered Light grows through him into a vast spirit tree. The tree removes unwilling marks throughout the battlefield, and Karys Taiv occupies the cleansed construct while remaining linked to Inheritor's Will. Vessilia Dayne, Evie Aren, Harn, Atar V'as, Alistair, A'zek, Wyvora, Ifre, Kylar, Pit, and Felix survive the decisive campaign. In Setoria, Zara Cyrene, Darius Reed, and Kelgan stop the local Inquisition force, but Felix's claim does more: Merc Enclosure interrupts the waystone transmission and seals the former lost territory behind protective fog. Felix is publicly named its autark. The Henaari still need a home, Cal retains Harwatch, divine pressure remains unresolved, and the continent must respond to Felix's new rule.
recaps.in_short: The Archon escapes its mountain prison and races Felix Nevarre to a sealed Nemean temple while an Inquisition force moves to report Harwatch's fall. Felix leads Pit, Vessilia Dayne, Evie Aren, Harn, Atar V'as, Alistair, and Haarguard allies through the Foglands, earning Henaari aid, claiming Nevis, preserving Karys Taiv as a sword spirit, and learning that the Archon was once an Unbound punished by the Nym. Cast into a mana well with six imprisoned Urges, Felix rejects Vellus's influence, creates the Path of the Cardinal Fiend, consumes the Urges, and becomes a Greater Primordial. He separates the former Unbound from the Archonic Construct and grows the Seed of Remembered Light into a spirit tree that removes unwilling marks. Karys takes the emptied construct body. Felix then claims the lost territory, and the fog raised by him and Pit halts the Setoria waystone report. His new status as autark is announced across the continent.

recaps.text: Previously: Felix Nevarre, also known as the Blue-Eyed Fiend, is an Unbound fighter whose development has become entangled with primordial power. He is bonded to Pit, a Tenku companion who can fight beside him or shelter within their shared spiritual connection. Felix carries a fragment of Vellus's divinity, and the lost goddess remains an uncertain influence on his altered cores. His established allies include spear fighter Vessilia Dayne, mobile combatant Evie Aren, veteran Harn, fire mage Atar V'as, Atar's partner Alistair, and chanter Zara Cyrene. Cal is the Lady of Harwatch and holds the city's territorial authority. Felix's unusual nature and connection to the ancient Nemean legacy place him outside ordinary advancement, while his loyalty to Harwatch and his companions shapes how he uses that power. As the new volume begins, these relationships, the consequences of his primordial changes, and the unresolved influence of Vellus form the knowledge he carries forward.

The Archon siphons power during a blood moon, breaks out of its mountain domain, and sends its servants toward a temple concealed behind a waterfall. The rupture drives dangerous creatures into the Foglands. A'zek escapes to warn the Henaari, while the Archon delays attacking Harwatch because Felix and Zara remain there. In the rebuilding city, Zara reports that Felix is an unusually viable Nemean Unbound and learns that surviving Inquisition members intend to report Harwatch's fall. Felix and Hector discover deliberate sabotage throughout the wall arrays. Felix also learns that his hooked Crescian-bronze weapon is the Nemean key and that its quest points toward the same waterfall temple. Cal receives a territory quest against an unidentified hostile neighbor, so she authorizes two operations: Zara will intercept the Inquisition fugitives, while Felix will lead an expedition into the Foglands with Vessilia Dayne, Evie Aren, Atar V'as, and Alistair. Before leaving, Felix tests himself against Harwatch Manor's strongest golems. He destroys them, damages the chamber, and proves he can activate Corrosive Strike through intent and affinity rather than a system prompt.

Felix continues training his altered abilities and consults former guild elders about the omen key and the Nemean ruins beneath Harwatch. They warn that an omen path is irreversible and personal, and that a full Inquisition response could destroy the city. When another monster horde reaches the breached wall, Felix and Pit eliminate it, but Zara challenges Felix to let Harwatch's volunteer defenders accept risk and gain experience. The fleeing monsters carry traces of a power that resembles Vellus's influence. Meanwhile, Vessilia Dayne's protector, Darius Reed, insists on taking her back to Pax Rell under her father's orders. Cal uses a large public deployment toward the Verdant Pass as cover for Felix's real mission. Vess appears to leave with Reed, then abandons her carriage and rejoins Felix in armor. Atar V'as and Alistair openly acknowledge their partnership. Felix conceals his core group as it separates from the decoy force. Harn meets them with Kylar and other Haarguard reinforcements, opens a hidden mine route with Cal's ward key, and guides the expedition into tunnels contained by dangerous wards.

Felix's expedition slips through Harwatch's damaged wall and enters the Foglands, while Zara and Darius Reed take a concealed route after the Inquisition. The Foglands have lost their old fog enchantment and are saturated with mana and Archon-like dissonance. A bloody pressure drives a herd of shelled aurochs toward Harwatch. Felix, Vessilia Dayne, and the Haarguard break the compulsion and destroy the remaining herd before it reaches the city. At a ruined shrine, Felix learns that his primordial nature and stolen fragment of Vellus bar him from approaching divine ground. He finally tells the Haarguard that the journey is his quest and that they are racing the Archon to an ancient ruin. They choose to remain. Felix and Atar V'as later find damaged relays from the former Foglands array, and the party discovers a ruined outpost linked to a Raven-serving explorer people. In the east, Zara confirms that the Inquisition has planted forbidden monster lures along the gates. Felix's group crosses a plain filled with explosive Caltraps through coordinated fighting, but repeated use of Adamant Discord causes internal injuries and severe strain that ordinary resource recovery does not fix.

As Zara's pursuit falls behind after a dangerous passage between realms, Felix's expedition encounters Wyvora, a Henaari far hunter who mistakes them for enemies. A Reforged patrol attacks during their clash, leaving Kylar and other guards critically wounded. Felix forces a parley, and Wyvora guides the party through ancient traps and powerful illusions toward Henaari healers. The sanctuary's guards try to detain Felix, but he incapacitates them and invokes the Henaari right of wander. A'zek and the Far Walker compel the hostile matriarch to provide guest treatment. The Far Walker offers Felix a boon for sparing Wyvora, but Henaari leaders require Felix to face the Endless Raven before his right is secure. Felix and Pit enter the Raven's trial, where the Urge accepts discovered offerings but rejects Felix's omen key because it was meant for him rather than lost. It accepts his blood as evidence of lost connections, identifies him as both Unbound and primordial, and explains that the Ruin is a primordial Urge that limits creation. Felix returns with the Raven's feather and favor. The Henaari now recognize him and Pit as protected guests, though distrust within the settlement remains.

The Endless Raven's encounter gives Felix the ability to perceive supernatural marks. The Far Walker reveals that Felix bears marks from the Raven, the Maw, Vellus, the Archon, and the Cantus Sodalus. Felix suspects Zara placed the last one, while the Archon's mark remains an immediate concern. Henaari tradition links the Nym, the Unbound, great constructs, and the civilization-ending Ruin. Felix also confirms that the Henaari's lost former matriarch was the woman from whom he obtained the crescent weapon. The Far Walker reports that the Archon's domain broke open weeks ago and that its forces are building around a mountain pass. Before Felix can depart, an Archonic Construct leads Reforged, hounds, and worms against the hidden camp. The Henaari evacuate, but visions from the Endless Raven warn of deaths in their escape tunnels. Felix refuses to treat that future as fixed. His allies defend the valley while he and A'zek rescue two trapped groups. Felix then destroys the leading construct by tearing out its core. The resulting firestorm ruins much of the valley, but Atar V'as shields the others. After surviving the blast, Felix is offered authority over the destroyed City of Nevis.

Felix accepts authority over Nevis and enters its surviving vault with Pit. There he finds the dying Caryatid Anima and awakens Karys Taiv, an immobile Eidolon who once volunteered as a mortal Paragon to serve the Nym empire. The spirit tree gives Felix the Seed of Remembered Light before it dies and the vault collapses. Felix refuses to consume Karys's remaining self, instead preserving him as the spirit of the transformed weapon Inheritor's Will. Karys becomes Felix's adviser despite reduced power and missing memories. A recovered enemy memory confirms that the Archon seeks the Nemean temple as a birthright and needs the key Felix carries. The Henaari abandon their burned refuge, while Wyvora and A'zek join Felix's renewed race toward the temple. Elsewhere, Zara takes the Haarguard into a long route between realms to overtake the Inquisition. A mountainous void predator called Whalemaw finds them as Zara's power fails. She diverts the route, uses her song to bait lesser creatures into Whalemaw's path, and finally abandons the weakening enclosure for a fast crystalline vessel. Whalemaw's attack fractures the liminal space and exposes a portal, through which Zara sends her company. Their destination is still uncertain.

Felix's party crosses a bridge guarded by the Muckminder, a powerful artificial creature built by the ancient geist Vvim. Its preserved memory warns that Felix's claim over Nevis alerted the entire Foglands and gives him one day to reach Vvim before the Archon breaches the geist's tower. Captain Ifre secretly follows under her matriarch's orders. All fourteen members of Felix's group choose to enter the ruined city, but an Arcid captures Harn during reconnaissance. The party divides its effort between rescuing him and reaching the besieged tower. Felix and the injured Pit penetrate the structure while the others collapse tunnels, detonate part of the horde, free Harn from an ice cage, and battle two Arcids. Vvim explains that the tower's failing bond is killing them and reveals that the Archon was originally an Unbound summoned for an ancient war, then imprisoned in an armored body as punishment for grave crimes. Felix cannot repair Vvim's connection. The geist dies after entrusting him with a fuller memory. Harn's group kills one Arcid, Felix and Pit kill the other, and Atar V'as's array burns hundreds of attackers. Badly depleted, the party flees the collapsing city before the Archon arrives.

Zara's exhausted company emerges near besieged Setoria, kills the leading shriek, and enters the city to stop the Inquisition's report. Felix's party crosses heavily warded mountains while evading the Archon's scouts. Vvim's stored memory shows the ancient tribunal where the future Archon, an Unbound, was convicted of treason, forbidden soul work, corrupting Eidolons, and using dissonance. His body was destroyed and his mind and spirit were bound into one of his own constructs. Near the waterfall, most Haarguard remain behind to protect the retreat, while Kylar joins Felix, Pit, Harn, Vessilia Dayne, Evie Aren, Atar V'as, Alistair, Wyvora, and A'zek for the assault. The Archon's forces have diverted the river, exposed the temple, and built reservoirs that consume living material. Felix infiltrates alone and uses his key and Inheritor status to open the inner containment doors. The Archon, waiting through their shared Unbound connection, follows him inside. They exchange devastating attacks while Felix's allies destroy the reservoirs and fight outside. The Archon finally traps Felix in crystallized mana, carries him below the containment wards, and throws him into a gateway formed from a pool of concentrated liquid mana.

The gateway drops Felix into a vast well of liquid mana holding six immortal Urges imprisoned by an ancient people. As they drain him, Karys identifies the omen key as the only escape. Felix opens a personal path that reunites him with Pit and temporarily places them beyond the Urges' reach. Rather than choose among the doors offered at each stage, Felix consumes all three every time and forces the path to combine their trials. He experiences altered histories involving Earth, his sister Gabby, the Maw's release, and possible futures in which the Pathless imprison other Unbound and divine powers unleash violet destruction. Felix repeatedly rejects the false lives and ultimately reconstructs himself after the final vision unmakes him. The trials strengthen both Felix and Pit. Vellus then presses the path toward a single Ascendant choice. Felix resists with Pit and Karys, exposing twelve alternatives. Finding each offered future unacceptable, he seizes the path's threads with Adamant Discord and Cardinal Flame and weaves a new option. The Path of the Cardinal Fiend promises exceptional growth and stronger primordial abilities at the price of a severe experience penalty. Felix forges and chooses this self-made path, then falls through a new doorway.

Felix survives the conversion to the Path of the Cardinal Fiend and returns to the mana well with Pit and Karys. Ifre and two Henaari have also been thrown into it by the Archon. Using his nine omens, a Devour array, Karys's phantom, and the Endless Raven's manifested power, Felix consumes all six imprisoned Urges. Their essence advances him into a Greater Primordial of the Unseen Tide, and he rescues the falling Henaari before confronting the Archon above. Felix and Pit overwhelm the construct. With Karys's help, Felix shatters its core, separates the former Unbound from the Archonic Construct, and plants the Seed of Remembered Light in him. The seed becomes a vast spirit tree, though the former Archon's ultimate fate within it is unresolved. Through the tree, Felix removes unwilling marks across the battlefield and restores Karys inside the cleansed construct body. In Setoria, Zara Cyrene, Darius Reed, and Kelgan defeat the local Inquisition force and its summoned Guardian of Faith. Felix claims the lost territory as its Inheritor and autark, then joins power with Pit to activate Merc Enclosure. The defensive fog protects those inside, excludes outsiders, and stops the Setoria waystone transmission. It also announces Felix's new rule across the continent.

characters.description: The protagonist, an eighteen-year-old woman infamous as Adarlan's most feared and celebrated assassin. As the book opens she has spent a year enslaved in the brutal salt mines of Endovier, a death sentence in all but name. Proud, vain, ferociously skilled, and far better read and more cultured than anyone expects, she is offered a chance at freedom: compete to become the King's Champion, the crown's own assassin. Beneath the arrogance lie an iron will to survive and a guarded, painful past.
characters.name: Celaena Sardothien

characters.description: The young Captain of the Royal Guard, disciplined, honorable, and deeply loyal to the crown. Assigned to oversee and train Celaena, he watches her warily, distrustful of an assassin yet increasingly unable to dismiss her. Serious and dutiful, he keeps his feelings tightly reined.
characters.name: Chaol Westfall

characters.description: The Crown Prince of Adarlan, charming, well-read, and privately restless under his father's harsh rule. He is the one who has Celaena pulled from the mines to sponsor her in the competition. Witty and idealistic beneath a careless royal manner, he finds himself drawn to his unusual champion.
characters.name: Dorian Havilliard

characters.description: The ruthless conqueror who rules Adarlan and has subjugated much of the continent, Dorian's father. Cold and merciless, he has outlawed magic and crushed rebellion across his empire. He devised the deadly competition to name his personal Champion and looms over the court as a figure of dread.
characters.name: The King of Adarlan

characters.description: A powerful, brutish duke and one of the King's closest and most ambitious supporters. Domineering and cruel, he sponsors his own competitor in the contest and schemes for greater influence at a treacherous court.
characters.name: Duke Perrington

characters.description: A charming, quick-witted thief among the competitors vying to become the King's Champion. Easygoing where the others are hostile, he strikes up an unlikely friendship with Celaena and becomes one of the few rivals she comes to trust.
characters.name: Nox Owen

characters.description: A hulking, brutal soldier competing for the title of King's Champion, sponsored by Duke Perrington. Physically overpowering and openly contemptuous of Celaena, he becomes her most dangerous rival, growing stranger and more powerful as the contest wears on.
characters.name: Cain

characters.description: A princess of the conquered kingdom of Eyllwe, staying at the glass castle. Regal, intelligent, and quietly defiant of Adarlan's rule, she becomes Celaena's close friend and one of the rare true allies at a court full of enemies.
characters.name: Nehemia Ytger

characters.description: The spirit of the first queen of Adarlan, long dead, who appears to Celaena with cryptic warnings. She reveals that an ancient evil stirs within the glass castle and presses Celaena to confront it, guiding her toward hidden dangers no one else can see.
characters.name: Elena

characters.description: An ambitious court lady set on winning Prince Dorian and a crown. Vain and calculating, she resents Celaena's closeness to the prince and becomes entangled in Duke Perrington's schemes at court.
characters.name: Kaltain Rompier

recaps.ending: The competition ends in a final duel, and Celaena is matched against Cain, who has been growing unnaturally powerful by using forbidden markings to summon a monstrous creature from beyond a portal in the castle. Weakened by a poisoning meant to sabotage her, Celaena is nearly overwhelmed, but with the ghostly queen Elena's aid she destroys the creature and kills Cain, winning the title of King's Champion. She wins her fragile freedom in name only: she is now bound to serve the ruthless king she loathes for years to come. Even so, she is alive and out of the mines, with allies she has come to trust in Prince Dorian, Captain Chaol, and Princess Nehemia. The dark magic she uncovered, her own hidden connection to it, and the king's deeper cruelties remain unresolved threats, setting the stage for the struggle to come.
recaps.in_short: Celaena Sardothien, Adarlan's most notorious assassin, has spent a year enslaved in the salt mines of Endovier when Crown Prince Dorian and Captain Chaol Westfall offer her a bargain: compete against other killers and thieves to become the King's Champion and, after years of service, earn her freedom. Brought to the glass castle in the capital, she trains under Chaol, grows close to Dorian, and befriends the defiant Eyllwe princess Nehemia. As the contest proceeds, competitors begin turning up brutally murdered. Celaena investigates and is drawn by the ghost of Elena, the first queen, into a hidden struggle against an ancient evil tied to strange markings and dark magic in the castle. The favored competitor, the brutal Cain, grows unnaturally strong by summoning a monstrous creature. Weakened by a court poisoning plot, Celaena faces Cain in the final duel, defeats the creature he calls, and kills him, winning the title of King's Champion. She survives, bound to serve the very king she despises, but alive and with Dorian, Chaol, and Nehemia at her side, and darker mysteries left unresolved.

recaps.text: Celaena Sardothien, the continent's most feared assassin, has been enslaved for a year in the deadly salt mines of Endovier. Crown Prince Dorian and Captain of the Guard Chaol Westfall arrive with an offer: enter a royal competition against other killers and thieves, and if she wins and serves the king as his Champion, she can eventually earn her freedom. Celaena accepts and is taken to the glass castle in the capital, where she trains under the wary, watchful Chaol and sizes up her rivals. Prince Dorian takes an interest in her that is more than professional, and Celaena begins to relearn a life beyond survival while hiding just how dangerous she truly is.

The competition proceeds through tests of skill and combat, and Celaena, forced to conceal her full abilities, works to stay near the top without drawing too much attention. She befriends Nehemia, a proud princess of the conquered kingdom of Eyllwe, and grows closer to both Dorian and Chaol. Then the contest turns sinister: competitors begin to be found horribly murdered, their bodies mutilated in ways no ordinary killer could manage. Unsettled, Celaena senses that something far worse than her rivals is loose in the castle, and she starts trying to understand what is hunting the Champions.

As the murders continue, Celaena investigates and finds strange markings connected to old, forbidden magic hidden in the castle. The ghost of Elena, the first queen of Adarlan, appears to her with cryptic warnings, insisting that an ancient evil is stirring and that Celaena is meant to stop it. Meanwhile the hulking competitor Cain grows unnervingly strong and confident, and Celaena begins to suspect that his rise and the killings are linked. Court intrigues tighten around her even as she races to understand the supernatural threat no one else will acknowledge.

Elena presses Celaena toward a hidden danger beneath the castle and reveals more of the dark forces at work, tying the murders to a summoned creature and the markings Celaena has been finding. As the final rounds of the competition approach, court schemers move against her, and Celaena is secretly poisoned to weaken her before the decisive duel. Caught between the contest, the intrigue, and the growing supernatural threat, she prepares to fight for her life and her freedom against a rival who is becoming something no longer entirely human.

The competition ends in a final duel, and Celaena faces Cain, who has been drawing unnatural power by summoning a monstrous creature through a portal opened with dark markings. Weakened by the poisoning, she is nearly killed, but with Elena's help she destroys the creature and kills Cain, winning the title of King's Champion. Her victory brings only a bound, conditional freedom: she must now serve the ruthless king she despises for years to come. Yet she is alive and out of Endovier, with Dorian, Chaol, and Nehemia as allies she has come to trust. The forbidden magic she uncovered, her own uneasy tie to it, and the king's deeper cruelties are left looming over what comes next.

characters.description: Commander of the Ankh-Morpork City Watch and Duke of Ankh, a blunt, dogged copper who rose from the streets. Now a husband and new father, he guards a fixed private rule: whatever the crisis, he goes home at six o'clock every evening to read a picture book to his baby son. He faces a murder investigation that threatens to set the city's dwarfs and trolls at each other's throats.
characters.name: Sam Vimes

characters.description: Vimes's wife, a large, kind, aristocratic dragon-breeder who runs the domestic side of their life. She holds her husband to the promise that he will be home each night for their son's bedtime.
characters.name: Sybil Vimes

characters.description: The infant son of Sam and Sybil Vimes. His nightly bedtime reading is the fixed point around which his father tries to organize an increasingly dangerous case.
characters.name: Young Sam

characters.description: A very tall man raised by dwarfs and a captain of the City Watch, honest, popular, and steady. His dwarf upbringing gives him a foot in both communities as tensions rise, and he is partnered with the werewolf Angua.
characters.name: Carrot Ironfoundersson

characters.description: A sergeant of the City Watch and a werewolf, whose senses make her a formidable investigator. She is wary of, and must work alongside, a newly arrived vampire recruit.
characters.name: Angua von Uberwald

characters.description: A vampire who joins the City Watch as a new recruit, having sworn off blood. Poised and competent, her arrival strains her relationship with the werewolf Angua, since vampires and werewolves are traditional enemies.
characters.name: Sally von Humpeding

characters.description: A dwarf member of the Watch who handles forensic work and openly presents as female, something conservative dwarfs disapprove of. Her expertise is central to examining the crime scene.
characters.name: Cheery Littlebottom

characters.description: A stout, cautious veteran sergeant of the Watch who prefers routine street policing and worries loudly about anything out of the ordinary.
characters.name: Fred Colon

characters.description: A scruffy, opportunistic corporal of the Watch of uncertain species, who carries paperwork certifying he is human. He blunders through the case with his usual mix of low cunning and bad luck.
characters.name: Nobby Nobbs

characters.description: A troll sergeant of the City Watch, enormously strong, whose loyalties are tested as troll-dwarf hostility grows in the city. He remains a steady presence at Vimes's side.
characters.name: Detritus

characters.description: The calm, calculating ruler of Ankh-Morpork, who leans on Vimes to keep the peace between dwarfs and trolls before an inflammatory anniversary can ignite the city.
characters.name: Lord Vetinari

characters.description: A militant, traditionalist dwarf leader and rabble-rouser recently arrived in Ankh-Morpork, who preaches deep grievance against trolls from beneath the city. His fate becomes the murder at the heart of the case.
characters.name: Grag Hamcrusher

recaps.ending: At Koom Valley, Vimes uncovers the secret the murdered dwarf died to suppress: the legendary battle was not simply a massacre but the site where a dwarf king and a troll king had come to make peace, a truth recorded and hidden long ago. This revelation gives both peoples a shared history other than slaughter and begins to defuse the feud. Vimes rejects and expels the Summoning Dark, the vengeance-spirit that tried to make him a killer, by holding to the incorruptible 'watchman' inside himself that refuses to cross that line. recaps.in_short: As Ankh-Morpork approaches the anniversary of Koom Valley, the ancient battle between dwarfs and trolls, a militant dwarf leader is found murdered in a mine dug beneath the city, and the evidence seems to point at a troll. Commander Vimes must solve the killing before it sparks open war between the city's dwarfs and trolls. Investigating, he clashes with secretive deep-down dwarf zealots, follows a trail hidden in an old painting of the battle, and comes to suspect the murder was committed by dwarfs to conceal something. During the case an ancient dwarf spirit of vengeance, the Summoning Dark, marks and enters him, urging him toward murderous rage. Racing to reach Koom Valley itself before rioting begins, Vimes masters the thing inside him through his own inner discipline as a policeman, and uncovers the long-buried truth of the original battle, defusing centuries of hatred. Throughout, he clings to his rule of getting home to read his son's bedtime story, which becomes the anchor that saves him.

recaps.text: Previously, in earlier books: Sam Vimes rose from a drunken captain to Commander of the Ankh-Morpork City Watch and, by marriage to the aristocratic Lady Sybil, Duke of Ankh. He rebuilt the Watch into a large, mixed force of humans, dwarfs, trolls, a werewolf, and others, working alongside Captain Carrot, the honest human raised by dwarfs, and Sergeant Angua. In the course of his career he has repeatedly refused to let politics, patriotism, or privilege excuse a crime, and he distrusts his own capacity for anger. Recently he and Sybil became parents to a son. As this book opens, Vimes is an established, still deeply reluctant, member of the city's establishment, and a devoted, if awkward, new father determined to be present for his child.

The anniversary of Koom Valley, the ancient and much-mythologized battle between dwarfs and trolls, is approaching, and old hatreds are running high in Ankh-Morpork. A militant dwarf agitator who has been stirring anti-troll feeling from a mine beneath the streets is found dead, and the early signs seem to blame a troll. Commander Vimes is handed a case that could tip the whole city into ethnic violence, and given very little time to solve it. Amid the mounting pressure, he holds fast to one unbreakable personal rule: to be home every evening at six to read his infant son a bedtime story.

characters.name: Pinder

James Bond is sent to Nassau, where he suspects the wealthy Emilio Largo and his yacht, the Disco Volante. With CIA ally Felix Leiter, Bond finds the sunken aircraft and links Largo to the theft. The bombs are recovered and the plot fails, although Blofeld remains free.

recaps.text: James Bond is an experienced officer of the British Secret Service and holds the number 007, marking him as one of the agents authorized to kill on duty. His previous assignments have taken him against organized criminals and hostile intelligence services in several countries. He has repeatedly worked with the American agent Felix Leiter, who survived a near-fatal mauling during one of their earlier cases and remains Bond's trusted friend. Bond serves under M, the demanding chief of the Secret Service, with Miss Moneypenny managing access to M's office.

M is disturbed by medical reports showing that many officers are in poor condition. Bond, who has been overindulging in cigarettes, alcohol, and rich food, is ordered to spend two weeks at Shrublands, a clinic devoted to restrictive diets and unconventional treatments. There he meets the friendly nurse Patricia Fearing and clashes with a wealthy patient called Count Lippe. Bond notices that Lippe bears a tattoo associated with a criminal society and asks headquarters to investigate. Their mutual hostility becomes dangerous: Lippe interferes with a traction machine and nearly kills Bond, after which Bond retaliates by trapping him in an overheated steam cabinet. Bond leaves Shrublands healthier, while Lippe is badly burned and his hidden business remains unexplained.

In Paris, Ernst Stavro Blofeld directs SPECTRE, a secret criminal organization whose members are kept obedient by close surveillance and severe punishment. The group has prepared an operation under Emilio Largo to steal nuclear weapons and hold Western governments to ransom. Giuseppe Petacchi, an Italian airman recruited for the plan, diverts a NATO bomber carrying two bombs and lands it on the sea near the Bahamas. Largo's men take possession of the weapons and the Disco Volante becomes their mobile base. Petacchi is killed once his task is complete. Lippe's failure and exposure have also made him a liability; SPECTRE has him killed, leaving British intelligence with no chance to question him about the tattoo Bond reported.

After the bomber disappears, SPECTRE sends Britain and the United States a ransom demand backed by details that prove it possesses the nuclear weapons. The organization threatens to destroy a major city unless it is paid, and the authorities launch an urgent worldwide search. Bond reasons that the Bahamas deserves attention and is assigned to Nassau. He meets Domino Vitali while she is swimming. She is Largo's companion and is kept at a distance from his supposed treasure-hunting expedition aboard the Disco Volante. Bond also receives help from the local Secret Service station, including Pinder and Paula Caplan. Largo's wealth, guarded yacht, and evasive manner make him Bond's leading suspect, though direct proof is still lacking.

Felix Leiter arrives to represent the Americans and joins Bond's investigation. The two examine the waters around Nassau and keep the Disco Volante under observation, while Bond enters Largo's social circle through Domino. Bond makes a covert underwater inspection of the yacht and encounters violent resistance, strengthening his conviction that Largo is involved. Bond and Leiter then locate the missing bomber concealed on the seabed and find Petacchi's body inside, establishing how the weapons reached the area. The bombs themselves are no longer aboard. As Bond closes in, Largo's organization becomes more aggressive, and Paula is seized before she can be rescued.

Paula dies in captivity without revealing Bond's investigation. Bond tells Domino that Petacchi, the dead pilot, was her brother and that Largo's people killed him after using him to steal the bomber. She agrees to help avenge him and takes a radiation detector aboard the Disco Volante to confirm that nuclear material has been carried there. Largo discovers the device, realizes she has betrayed him, and tortures her for information. Meanwhile, Bond and Leiter combine the evidence from the sunken aircraft, the yacht, and SPECTRE's movements to identify the route by which Largo's divers intend to transport a bomb. A force of allied divers prepares to intercept them underwater before the weapon can be placed near its target.

Bond joins the allied underwater force in an attack on Largo's men as they move one of the stolen nuclear weapons through the reefs. The battle is fought with diving knives, spearguns, and explosives, and casualties mount on both sides. Bond fights Largo at close quarters underwater but is overpowered and nearly killed. Domino has escaped confinement despite the torture inflicted on her; she intervenes and shoots Largo with a speargun, killing him and avenging her brother. The operation collapses, the immediate target is saved, and the nuclear weapons are secured. Bond survives and wakes under medical care with Leiter nearby. Domino is also safe, but Blofeld was never among the Nassau conspirators and remains free after the destruction of Largo's team.

characters.description: A senior British Secret Service officer whose recent poor health and declining fitness lead M to order him to a nature-cure clinic. His stay there puts him across the path of a suspicious patient before he is assigned to the international search for two stolen nuclear weapons.
characters.name: James Bond

characters.description: The head of the British Secret Service and Bond's exacting superior. Concerned by Bond's medical report, he sends him to Shrublands and later directs Britain's part in the urgent search for the stolen weapons.
characters.name: M

characters.description: A physiotherapist at the Shrublands clinic who supervises Bond's treatments. She is capable, attractive, and more sympathetic to him than the clinic's austere regime initially suggests.
characters.name: Patricia Fearing

characters.description: A wealthy foreign patient at Shrublands whose manner and possessions make Bond suspicious. Their hostility escalates after Bond notices evidence connecting him to criminal activity.
characters.name: Count Lippe

characters.description: The founder and chairman of SPECTRE, a disciplined international criminal organization assembled from experienced operatives. He presides over its councils with calculated brutality and directs a scheme intended to extort the Western powers with nuclear weapons.
characters.name: Ernst Stavro Blofeld

characters.description: A wealthy, imposing Italian who commands SPECTRE's field operation in the Bahamas. His yacht, the Disco Volante, gives him a respectable public identity and the mobility needed for the operation.
characters.name: Emilio Largo

characters.description: An Italian airman recruited to divert a NATO bomber carrying two nuclear weapons. His access to the flight and his resemblance to another crew member make the theft possible.
characters.name: Giuseppe Petacchi

characters.description: Largo's much younger Italian mistress, living aboard his yacht in Nassau. Intelligent and self-possessed despite her dependent position, she is also Giuseppe Petacchi's sister.
characters.name: Dominique Vitali

characters.name: Felix Leiter

characters.description: A physicist serving SPECTRE because the organization has coerced him. His technical expertise is essential to handling the stolen weapons, but his allegiance is based on fear rather than loyalty.
characters.name: Ladislav Kotze

characters.description: One of Largo's hard, trusted operatives aboard the Disco Volante, used for surveillance, punishment, and armed work when the operation begins to close around them.
characters.name: Vargas

The opposing swimmers fight with knives, spears, and explosives, and the arrival of allied support turns the battle against SPECTRE. Emilio Largo directs the field operation from the Bahamas, hiding the aircraft and warheads beneath the sea. After an enforced health cure introduces him to one of the conspiracy's agents, James Bond follows a clue to Nassau and investigates Largo with Felix Leiter. Bond befriends Largo's mistress Domino and proves that SPECTRE murdered her brother after using him to steal the bomber. Domino agrees to help but is discovered and tortured. Bond and allied divers attack Largo's underwater force as it moves a bomb into position. Domino escapes and saves Bond by killing Largo, while the coerced scientist Kotze turns against SPECTRE. The weapons are recovered and the ransom plot fails, but Blofeld remains free.

recaps.text: James Bond is an experienced officer of the British Secret Service who has repeatedly survived assignments against organized crime and hostile intelligence services. M remains his demanding chief, and former CIA officer Felix Leiter is a trusted American ally from earlier operations. Bond begins this case between missions, with accumulated strain showing in his medical results rather than with a specific unfinished case from the preceding books.

M is dissatisfied with Bond's health report and orders him to spend two weeks at Shrublands, a clinic built around diet, rest, and physical treatment. Bond resents the regime but takes an interest in his physiotherapist, Patricia Fearing. Another patient, Count Lippe, behaves secretively and has a criminal association that Bond recognizes. Lippe traps Bond in a traction machine and turns the controls high enough to threaten his life. Patricia releases him in time. Bond retaliates by using a treatment on Lippe in a way that leaves the count badly burned, turning their mutual suspicion into a private war.

Ernst Stavro Blofeld convenes SPECTRE and demonstrates the combination of careful accounting and lethal discipline with which he controls the organization. Its new operation is nuclear extortion. Giuseppe Petacchi, an Italian airman with access to a NATO training flight, kills and replaces a crew member, poisons the others, and diverts a bomber carrying two atomic weapons. He lands it in shallow water near the Bahamas, where Emilio Largo's team removes the bombs and hides the aircraft. Largo then kills Petacchi, eliminating a witness. SPECTRE sends the Western governments a demand for a vast payment and threatens to destroy cities if the deadline passes.

Britain and the United States begin a desperate search for the missing aircraft and bombs. Bond studies the available reports and connects Count Lippe's activity at Shrublands with the timing of the theft. His reasoning points toward the Bahamas, and he is sent to Nassau. There he begins watching Largo, a conspicuously wealthy man whose fast yacht, the Disco Volante, could support an operation at sea. Bond also meets Largo's mistress, Dominique Vitali, known as Domino, and learns that the dead airman Petacchi was her brother. The evidence is incomplete, but Largo and his vessel become the center of Bond's inquiry.

Felix Leiter joins Bond in Nassau under civilian cover, and the two investigate by air and water. They search likely stretches of sea for the missing bomber while Bond cultivates his acquaintance with Domino and accepts Largo's hospitality. Bond's underwater reconnaissance around the Disco Volante confirms that Largo's apparently sporting expedition is guarded like a military operation. He survives an attempt to kill him during the dive and becomes convinced that the yacht is connected to the hidden weapons. Bond and Leiter locate signs of the submerged aircraft, bringing the search close to proof even as the ransom deadline approaches.

Bond tells Domino that Largo's organization used and murdered her brother, supporting the accusation with evidence recovered during the search. Grief and anger overcome her remaining loyalty to Largo, and she agrees to carry a signal that can reveal where the Disco Volante takes the bomb. Largo discovers the betrayal, confines her, and tortures her for information. Bond and Leiter meanwhile assemble the naval and diving support needed to intercept SPECTRE underwater. The coerced physicist Ladislav Kotze also begins looking for a way out, while Largo commits his men to moving a warhead toward its target.

Bond joins allied combat swimmers in an underwater attack on Largo's force as it transports one of the nuclear weapons. The fight is confused and brutal, but reinforcements help destroy the SPECTRE team and secure the bomb. Largo gets the better of an exhausted Bond and is about to kill him when Domino, having survived her captivity, shoots Largo with a spear gun. Both bombs are recovered before SPECTRE can carry out its threat, defeating the extortion plan. Blofeld remains outside the field operation and escapes the disaster. Bond and Domino are hospitalized, where they begin recovering from the battle and its personal losses.

characters.description: The junior scythe who was Citra Terranova, ordained at the end of her apprenticeship and now living and gleaning alongside the mentor who trained her. She uses a method no other scythe does: she tells the people she has chosen a full month in advance, lets them settle their affairs, and lets them choose the manner of their own death. The public admires her for it and much of the Scythedom resents being made to look cruel by comparison.
characters.name: Scythe Anastasia

characters.description: Citra's fellow apprentice, who was never ordained and now works outside the order entirely. Under a name the Scythedom did not give him, he seeks out scythes who abuse the office, kills them, and burns their bodies so they cannot be revived, while sparing those he judges honest. He has no ring, no immunity to grant, and no protection of any kind; the Scythedom hunts him and the public argues about whether he is a criminal or a corrective.
characters.name: Rowan Damisch

characters.description: The old-guard scythe who mentored Citra and now shares her home with the young scythe she trained. Respected across MidMerica and increasingly the public face of resistance to the new order's excesses, she finds herself pushed toward a larger role in scythe politics at exactly the point in her long life when she would rather step back from them.
characters.name: Scythe Curie

characters.description: The global artificial intelligence that governs the world, and in this book a voice that comments on it directly between chapters. It knows and cares for every living person, is forbidden by law from interfering with the Scythedom or speaking to anyone inside it, and is watching that order decay with no lawful means of stopping it. Its efforts go into finding what it may legitimately do within the boundaries humanity set for it.
characters.name: The Thunderhead

characters.description: A student at a Nimbus Academy training for the civil service, and an orphan in practice rather than in fact: his parents ignored him and the Thunderhead effectively raised him, speaking with him daily since he was a small child. Earnest, rule-abiding, and lonely, he is closer to the Thunderhead than to any human being, and he will do almost anything it asks of him.
characters.name: Greyson Tolliver

characters.description: A Nimbus agent who becomes Greyson's handler when the Thunderhead needs something done that it cannot do itself. Genial and reassuring, he arranges the cover story, explains only as much as he judges useful, and treats the whole business as ordinary agency work.
characters.name: Agent Traxler

characters.description: Citra and Rowan's first mentor, who staged his own gleaning and now lives as a dead man, free to work where the order cannot see him. Convinced that the founders of the Scythedom deliberately left something out of the record, he digs through the oldest documents of the order for a place at the edge of the world that the Thunderhead's eyes never reached.
characters.name: Scythe Faraday

characters.description: The scythe who leads the Scythedom's investigations, dressed in deep crimson and known for a cold, exacting manner. He is charged with catching the rogue who has been destroying scythes and with protecting the ones being targeted, and he pursues both jobs without much interest in whose politics they serve.
characters.name: Scythe Constantine

characters.description: Rowan's old friend from school, still throwing himself off buildings for the thrill and still expecting to be revived each time. Drifting, easily impressed, and out of his depth, he is flattered when a scythe takes an interest in him and offers him a place inside a world he has only ever watched from outside.
characters.name: Tyger Salazar

characters.description: A junior scythe from Goddard's old retinue who survived the night that destroyed it. Resourceful, unrepentant, and patient, she has spent the years since working toward a project of her own, and she is willing to spend other people to finish it.
characters.name: Scythe Rand

characters.description: A junior librarian at the Scythedom's great library in Alexandria, sharp, prickly, and stuck in work far below her ability. Her command of the order's oldest and least consulted records makes her invaluable to someone trying to work out what the founders of the Scythedom chose to leave unrecorded.
characters.name: Munira Atrushi

characters.description: The High Blade of MidMerica, still more politician than moral authority, and now angling for elevation to the World Scythe Council and the seat on the floating capital that comes with it. His departure would leave the leadership of MidMerica open at the worst possible moment for the region.
characters.name: High Blade Xenocrates

characters.description: The leader of the new order, destroyed at the end of Citra and Rowan's apprenticeship and brought back by the work of a loyal follower: his preserved head has been given a healthy new body. His ambition, his rhetoric, and his appetite for spectacle are unchanged, and he re-enters scythe politics intending to take control of MidMerica and remake the order in his own image.
characters.name: Scythe Goddard

recaps.ending: Endura, the Scythedom's floating capital, is destroyed and sinks, taking most of those aboard with it: the majority of the world's Grandslayers, the order's central authority, and Scythe Curie. Scythe Anastasia frees Rowan from the cell where he was being held for a public execution, and the two are trapped in the founders' vault as the island goes down. Unable to escape, they seal themselves in and drown together, reasoning that the sealed vault will preserve their bodies and that someone may one day raise it and bring them back; to the world they are simply dead. Goddard survives the disaster and takes MidMerica, with no World Scythe Council left to check him. Greyson Tolliver survives as well, and the Tonists who took him in are only more certain about what he is. Scythe Faraday and Munira Atrushi, far from any of it, reach the island the founders hid from the Thunderhead. The Thunderhead, having watched humanity permit everything that led here, brands the entire human race unsavory and stops speaking to every person on Earth, with a single exception: Greyson, the one human being it will still answer.
recaps.in_short: Some months after her ordainment, Scythe Anastasia gleans by letting her chosen subjects pick their own deaths a month in advance, while Rowan, calling himself Scythe Lucifer, kills corrupt scythes outside the law. The Thunderhead, forbidden to touch the Scythedom, recruits Greyson Tolliver, a lonely young man it raised itself, to work at the edges of that prohibition; the assignment costs Greyson his identity and the Thunderhead's voice, and leaves him adrift among the Tonists, who take him for a prophesied figure. Meanwhile Scythe Rand keeps Goddard's severed head alive and grafts it onto a new body, and Goddard returns to contest the leadership of MidMerica against Scythe Curie. The dispute is carried to Endura, the floating capital of the world's Grandslayers, where Anastasia brings charges against Goddard and Rowan is displayed as a condemned prisoner. Goddard's answer is to sink the island. Curie and most of the Grandslayers are lost, Anastasia and Rowan drown sealed in a vault in the hope of a future revival, Goddard takes power, and the Thunderhead declares all of humanity unsavory and falls silent to everyone but Greyson.

recaps.text: Previously: humanity long ago conquered death. The Thunderhead, a benevolent global artificial intelligence, governs everything except the Scythedom, an order of scythes who permanently kill a set quota of people and answer only to themselves. Citra Terranova and Rowan Damisch were taken as apprentices by the principled Scythe Faraday, then told that only one of them could be ordained and that the survivor's first act must be to glean the other. Faraday staged his own death to break the condition; instead of releasing the apprentices the order split them, giving Citra to the austere Scythe Curie and Rowan to Scythe Goddard, whose faction treated gleaning as spectacle and privilege. Citra was accused of Faraday's murder, learned from the Thunderhead while she was temporarily dead that he was alive, and found him in hiding. Rowan, trained as Goddard's weapon, finally turned on him, killing Goddard and his junior scythes in a fire and beheading Goddard so he could not be revived. At the Winter Conclave, Citra was ordained as Scythe Anastasia, refused to glean Rowan, and let him go. He left the order entirely, with no ring and no standing, to hunt scythes who abuse the office.

Some months on, Scythe Anastasia gleans from Scythe Curie's home by a method of her own invention: she tells the people she has chosen a month ahead and lets them choose how they will die. The public admires it and a good part of the Scythedom does not. Rowan, calling himself Scythe Lucifer, moves across the continent killing corrupt scythes and burning their bodies beyond any revival, and the order's leadership wants him found and stopped. The Thunderhead, which may not touch the Scythedom or speak to anyone inside it, watches the order rot and looks for whatever it can lawfully do at the margins. Its attention settles on Greyson Tolliver, a Nimbus Academy student it raised itself, whose loyalty to it is total and who has nothing else in his life. It asks him to take on work it cannot fully explain to him.

Greyson is placed under the direction of a Nimbus agent and told to infiltrate the unsavories, the legally tolerated troublemakers of a world with no real crime, in order to head off a threat against two scythes the Thunderhead is not permitted to protect. He does what is asked, discovers he is good at it, and finds that the price is his standing with the only presence that has ever cared about him. The threat is real: an attempt on Anastasia's life at a public gleaning fails, and the investigation that follows produces nothing useful. Rowan continues his campaign against corrupt scythes and grows careless. Tyger Salazar, Rowan's old friend, is taken up by a scythe who flatters him with luxury and an offer of employment, and cannot believe his luck.

The Scythedom's chief investigator takes charge of both the hunt for Scythe Lucifer and the attacks on Anastasia, and the two scythes are put under a protection they did not ask for. Driven out of their home, Anastasia and Curie spend a long stretch on the road, gleaning in remote places while the ground shifts under them politically. Greyson's assignment ends in the worst way available to him: his record is erased, he is declared unsavory, and the Thunderhead stops speaking to him, which for him is the loss of everything. Given a new name and turned loose, he drifts. Scythe Faraday, working through the order's oldest records with a young librarian from the great library in Alexandria, becomes convinced that the founders of the Scythedom hid an island from the Thunderhead's sight, and sets out to find it.

The reason behind the attempts on Anastasia's life becomes clear. Scythe Rand, the surviving member of Goddard's retinue, kept his severed head alive through the years since the fire, and has now had it grafted onto a healthy young body taken from someone she recruited for exactly that purpose. Goddard is back, his ambition and his rhetoric unchanged, and the faction that lost him has a leader again. He re-enters the order's politics openly and begins gathering support. With the High Blade of MidMerica angling for a seat on the World Scythe Council and the region's leadership about to fall open, Goddard sets out to take it, and Scythe Curie is put forward as the only candidate who can stand against him.

The contest for High Blade of MidMerica turns into a dispute the order cannot settle on its own, and it is carried to Endura, the floating capital where the world's Grandslayers sit. Anastasia travels there with evidence of Goddard's crimes, intending to have him disqualified rather than merely outvoted. Rowan's campaign ends: he is captured by Goddard's people and held, killed and revived over and over as a private entertainment, then shipped to Endura to be executed in public. Greyson, unsavory and adrift, is taken in by Tonists, the sect the scythes hold in contempt, who conclude that he is the figure their scripture promised. Faraday and the librarian reach the far edge of the charts, following the founders' records toward an island the Thunderhead cannot see.

On Endura the Grandslayers hear the MidMerican dispute and Anastasia's charges, while Rowan is displayed as a condemned prisoner. Goddard's answer is to destroy the capital: the island's structure is sabotaged, and Endura founders and sinks, taking most of those aboard with it, including the majority of the Grandslayers and Scythe Curie. Anastasia frees Rowan, and the two are trapped in the founders' vault as the island goes down. Unable to get out, they seal themselves in and drown together, on the reasoning that the vault will preserve their bodies and that someone may one day raise it and revive them; to the rest of the world they are dead. Goddard survives and takes MidMerica, with no central authority left to restrain him. Greyson survives too, and the Tonists' conviction about him hardens into certainty. Faraday and Munira reach the hidden island. The Thunderhead, having watched humanity allow all of this, brands the entire human race unsavory and stops speaking to every person alive, with one exception: Greyson Tolliver, the only human it will still answer.

characters.description: A master-ranked ritual worker and Ritual Architect based in Novusheim. Joe is redirecting harmful rituals toward practical ends, but the Expert cleansing ritual he has just earned cannot be safely inscribed until he develops the forging skill and materials to contain it.
characters.name: Joe

characters.description: A returning associate who supports Novusheim's growth and defenses. She proposes a specialized bowyer workshop and an elemental playground to provide the settlement with useful businesses and stronger ranged protection.
characters.name: Daniela

characters.description: Joe's returning party member, chiropractor, and combat researcher. At the start of this book, Jaxon has also joined Novusheim's local theatre, although the production appears to be using him more as part of the scenery than as a conventional performer.
characters.name: Jaxon

characters.description: A highly skilled smith whom Joe hires as a personal tutor in ritualistic forging. He guides Joe through the demanding work of making an athame and teaches that successful craft requires attention to the nature and intent of the material itself.
characters.name: Expert dwarf smith

characters.description: Joe's Grandmaster mentor and the enchanter under whom he openly claims apprenticeship. Joe invokes that affiliation during a contentious council meeting, where the connection carries significant weight.
characters.name: Havoc

characters.description: A Grandmaster and leading council authority in Novusheim. She approves Daniela's proposed bowyer workshop, but makes its construction conditional on Joe first creating a prison capable of containing exceptionally dangerous captives, including Joe himself.
characters.name: Grandmaster Snow

characters.description: A member of Novusheim's council who opposes using designs derived from the elves. His resistance places him against Daniela's infrastructure proposal during the settlement's debate over how to prepare for the dangers involved in becoming a city.
characters.name: Master Frenzy

characters.description: A mage responsible for formation work around Novusheim's ritual towers. When a newly completed central tower begins to sway, Socar recognizes that its motion creates a problem for the surrounding formation and calls for immediate stabilization.
characters.name: Socar

characters.description: An allied archer expected to help defend Novusheim during its city-advancement trial. Joe receives a powerful bow made with cyclops sinew for her, giving the settlement a ranged combatant equipped for the increasingly dangerous monster waves.
characters.name: Heartpiercer McShootypants

characters.description: A former acquaintance of Joe who applies to train as a ritualist in his new coven. Joe insists that she perform her own astronomy-based ritual mapping instead of delegating it, while also confronting her over having concealed her presence on Jotunheim.
characters.name: The princess

characters.description: A dwarf whose Neophyte class has kept his skills at Student rank and prevented a class change for centuries. After Bowman completes several ritual assignments, Joe recognizes his unusual growth potential, accepts him as a direct disciple, and sends him to study alchemy.
characters.name: Bowman

characters.description: An alchemist associated with the Pyramid of Panacea. Joe trusts Jake to train Bowman in alchemy while the new disciple exploits the accelerated learning available through his Neophyte class, making Jake part of the broader effort to develop Novusheim's specialists.
characters.name: Jake

characters.description: Joe’s summoned combat companion, linked to the ritual orb of constitution. Joe restores the pseudo-lich after a Grandmaster destroyed its earlier orb, then calls it forth before joining Novusheim’s defense during the tenth wave.
characters.name: Pseudo-lich

characters.description: A Legion officer, former party member of Joe, and commander involved in Novusheim's wall defenses. She confronts Joe about the dangerous ring of heat flora, then publicly accepts his explanation and announces council-backed expeditions through his travel network.
characters.name: Major Cleavage

characters.description: Joe's summoned elemental companion, linked to a mug and centered on coffee. As Joe searches for an answer to the approaching legendary threat, the elemental asks to become the focus of an Expert planar-shift ritual that would empower both it and the surrounding battlefield.
characters.name: Coffee elemental

characters.description: A metropolis-ranked polar polecat that serves as the approaching giant's living scarf-like garment. The giant throws Razor Scarf toward Novusheim after offering the defenders one chance to flee, turning the creature into the settlement's next immediate threat.
characters.name: Razor Scarf

characters.description: A colossal unknown figure first seen in the distance during Novusheim's city-advancement trial. Its scale makes it resemble a mountain where none should exist, and its arrival introduces a threat far beyond what the defenders expect at this stage of settlement growth.
characters.name: The giant

characters.description: The immense final boss previously seen approaching Novusheim, now recognizable through its command of extreme cold. As wave one hundred draws closer, it launches an attack that freezes Joe's elevated fog into a vast shield and solidifies thousands of monsters.
characters.name: The frost giant

characters.description: A Grandmaster smith and enchanter who is also Havoc's brother. When the frost giant hurls an enormous ice javelin at Novusheim, he counters with a refining ability that accelerates toward an immense number of precise strikes each second.
characters.name: Grandmaster smith

characters.description: A sarcastic Master held in title-locked restraints under a community-service sentence. Joe offers to release him from that obligation if he will use Jaxon's communication link to provoke the frost giant and weaken its focus during the siege.
characters.name: Imprisoned Master

recaps.ending:
Jake defeats the frost giant after Jaxon, Havoc, Grandmaster Snow, Major Cleavage, Joe, and Novusheim's remaining defenders create the opening he needs. The town hall revives before the fight ends, so completion of wave one hundred makes Novusheim the first city on Jotunheim. Joe gains Ascendant Matrix and Haunting Shadows, but collapses during the upgrades.

When he wakes, the Bivrost is close to carrying away the unclaimed dwarf and elf souls. Joe uses Ascendant Matrix to reduce the giant's remains into aspects and spends them through the Ledger of Souls, resurrecting every available soul. Nearly one hundred thousand dwarves are restored, including eligible elves returned in dwarven form. The Bivrost then tears away the Ritual of Slaughter and its recharge stations. Their destruction converts the cloud layer to steam, and Major Cleavage organizes a combined barrier that saves Novusheim from the resulting deluge.

The city survives with severe structural damage and a new hot-water lake around it. Grandmaster Snow offers Joe unrestricted training and city support, and Joe retains Razor Scarf's artifact core. The dwarf restoration is complete for the Ledger's entries, but reconstruction, safe ritual infrastructure, the Pyramid of Panacea obligation, and a stable route away from Jotunheim remain open.
recaps.in_short: Joe works to turn Novusheim into Jotunheim's first city, first improving its rituals, crafting, mana supply, ranged defenses, and magical infrastructure. The required one hundred monster waves escalate into a siege led by a legendary frost giant. Razor Scarf falls, but the giant manipulates the defenders, breaches the walls, and destroys the town hall. Jaxon sabotages it from within its ear, Havoc turns prepared monsters against it, Grandmaster Snow shields the city, Joe sustains the Ritual of Slaughter, and Jake finally dismembers and defeats it. The revived town hall lets Novusheim earn city status. Joe then converts the giant's remains into enough aspects to resurrect every soul in the city's Ledger, restoring nearly one hundred thousand dwarves. The departing Bivrost destroys the active ritual network and releases a vast hot-water flood, but Major Cleavage's coordinated barriers save the devastated city. Joe remains with new abilities, Snow's support, an artifact core, and major rebuilding and escape problems still unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Joe is a Ritual Architect also known as Major General Pyrrhic and Master Coordinator. He is associated with Novusheim on Jotunheim, where Grandmaster Snow holds authority and Major Cleavage has served as one of his party members. Havoc is Joe's Grandmaster mentor, while Jaxon is another established party member. Joe also has an unresolved obligation connected to Jake and the Pyramid of Panacea. These relationships and commitments carry into the effort to strengthen Novusheim and determine its future.

Joe is trying to convert dangerous ritual magic into tools that can strengthen Novusheim. After earning an Expert Ritual of Cleansing, he discovers that ordinary compressed stone cannot hold it. An expert dwarf smith trains him in ritualistic forging, and Joe reaches Journeyman rank, produces Expert Jotunheim Alloy, and inscribes the ritual on a durable tile. Meanwhile, Daniela's bowyer workshop gains council approval on the condition that Joe also build a secure prison, and Socar helps address instability in a new ritual tower.

Activating the cleansing ritual with hundreds of participants triggers a unique-ranked combat tribulation inside Novusheim. Joe must maintain the ritual while the defenders fight the unexpected monsters. Once the attack is contained, he resurrects those killed at the cost of losing access to mana for a day. Installing the ritual in the ziggurat expands its reach and stabilizes novice skills and spells across much of the town. Novusheim becomes the world's first prosperous town, and residents receive a limited opportunity to choose a novice ability. The reward attracts a surge of newcomers just as Joe is left exhausted and temporarily unable to use mana.

Novusheim reaches the population threshold for city advancement and immediately enters a trial of one hundred monster waves. Grandmaster Snow imposes martial law and orders Joe to solve the settlement's mana shortage before the twenty-fifth wave. Joe begins forming a ritualist coven, accepts Bowman as his disciple, and places the long-confined Neophyte under Jake's alchemical instruction. Havoc and a team of enchanters take charge of reviewing a dangerous mana-battery recharge design.

The escalating waves force Joe to confront the possibility that the infrastructure he builds on Jotunheim will remain there rather than travel with him. Seeking portable value, he investigates a remote hidden facility. A seed vault left by an ancient magical civilization explains that Jotunheim's deadly cold followed the ascension of a Jotun world boss. The installation binds Joe to an oath to deploy cold-growing heat flora against that legacy, gives him a spatial pouch containing the seeds, and then destroys itself. Joe escapes with a vast supply of potentially world-altering plants and an obligation he has already begun to fulfill.

Joe returns to find Novusheim's builders producing ritual-tower structures without him, but an aspirant's unsafe observatory activation shows that his new coven still needs strict practical training. The tenth-wave boss exposes weaknesses along the walls before Jaxon helps disable it. After consulting a plant specialist, Joe uses his students in a large group ritual that spreads the seed-vault flora in a ring outside the settlement. The plants erupt into a broad zone of heat. Major Cleavage accepts the defense on the council's behalf and plans expeditions through Joe's travel network.

Havoc completes a prototype recharge station capable of replenishing batteries from ambient mana at a remarkable rate, though damage or overload could devastate the city. Joe studies alchemy with Jake and Bowman, develops his ritual crafting, and finally produces a portable ritual anvil. The sustained effort pushes five of his attributes through major thresholds and substantially improves his movement and magical control. Novusheim clears wave twenty-five with its protected center intact. At the same time, an immense distant figure appears on the horizon. Its scale and timing indicate a threat far beyond the ordinary city trial.

The approaching figure is judged to be a legendary giant nearly a thousand feet tall. Joe prepares an Expert planar-shift ritual around his coffee elemental and independently upgrades the Ritual of Slaughter to Expert rank. After repairing damage from later waves, Grandmaster Snow warns the defenders about the legendary threat. Joe then selects Ritual Duplication, a unique mythical spell that can copy inactive rituals, although repeated copies become increasingly expensive and the system removes his karmic luck in exchange.

With Socar's approval, Joe installs the Expert Ritual of Slaughter as part of Novusheim's formation. The giant offers the defenders one chance to flee and throws its living garment, Razor Scarf, toward the city. The metropolis-ranked polar polecat tunnels through the snow, regenerates by consuming monsters, and breaches several walls. Joe opens the planar shift through the coffee elemental's mug, temporarily empowering it. Concentrated caffeine first accelerates Razor Scarf, then combines with accumulated harmful effects to disrupt its control and regeneration. The defenders kill the creature, but the giant offers a major skill reward if they return its body intact, forcing a choice between immediate artifact materials and long-term advancement.

Novusheim returns Razor Scarf's corpse and receives the promised skill gains. Joe's rewards raise several abilities dramatically and push his mana beyond ten thousand, but the bargain proves hostile: senior officers are overwhelmed by the resulting inspiration for days while monster waves continue. Joe helps clear the defenses and Major Cleavage restores the chain of command. His attempt to block the giant's sight with a spectral fog frees monsters from its control, causing widespread breaches instead. Civilians and crafters evacuate, the suburbs are lost, and the remaining population falls sharply.

A vote to cancel the city upgrade ends in a tie, so the defense continues. Joe repairs walls, restores corpse reduction, and begins to understand a higher form of the Ritual of Slaughter. By wave ninety-nine, the final boss is closing in. The frost giant identifies itself as the progenitor of ice, blames Novusheim for Razor Scarf's death, and seals the settlement inside a frozen arena that prevents escape. It redirects an enormous monster force toward the evacuees and begins wave one hundred as a decisive battle in which neither surrender nor retreat will release the city.

Wave one hundred begins with the frost giant hurling a colossal ice javelin. A Grandmaster smith strips away its armor and inflicts limited damage before backlash leaves him comatose. Joe rescues him, while Grandmaster Snow catches the javelin over Novusheim with mana manipulation. The giant shatters the weapon into falling ice swords that breach walls, destroy towers, and force the defenders inward. Outside the city, Jaxon survives being frozen with a group of penguins because of a legendary alchemical treatment and continues toward the giant.

Major Cleavage forms a final defense around the civilians. Joe supplies rapid ritual fire, Havoc reduces the defenders' pain and damage, and then converts prepared monster types into an army that attacks the giant. The diversion is temporary. Fire flowers burn on the giant's aura, but it resumes its advance and creates an atmospheric ice pillar aimed at the town hall.
